non_blocking_findings: Production seam in demos/ship_consoles.gd is a visible behaviour change. Base code mid-transit: select -> map.select no-op (no card), cancel -> press_cancel queues a cancel that only reaches the sim on the next journey tick, commit -> open_commit_dialog false -> misleading card 'Plot a course first'. Seam sends the intent immediately with dt 0.0 and shows the sim's committed refusal card. It is a player-visible improvement and the plan's AC3 needs it, but the plan said no seams; record it as a deliberate product change in the changelog/ledger. Intents are recorded as normal input lines (dtau 0.0), identical across runs, so determinism holds; replay of dt 0 inputs is not exercised until M4.6gR3.

Seam edge case: select with arg 'Sol' while committed returns false silently (index_of('Sol') < 0) while the non-committed path treats Sol as plan_home. Also unknown-target select returns false with no card. Proposed fix: send plan_home-equivalent or show the refusal card for 'Sol' and unknown ids.

Cost: 373k check() calls, ~135 MB display_samples.ndjson per run and ~90-100 s per playthrough (adversarial ~180 s, title/negative extra). ship-demo-ci grows by roughly 5-6 min. Count is noise, not a defect; consider running D-68 text checks per phase/on text change instead of per frame and sampling bindings every Nth frame.

Pole assertion is camera-aimed by the driver and the max offset (0.077606201 px) is identical in all three phases, so it checks the sim heading -> camera.heading -> Camera3D projection chain only at one fixed heading; it does not exercise changing headings. Acceptable for R-M4.3b-1 CPU half; GPU half is M4.6gR3.
Executor claimed 148 s wall; measured 102 s and 90 s (not a concern). All other claims matched exactly.
